A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their complete main text, equations, Algorithm 1, Tables 1–9, Figures 1–4 and Appendices A–F support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original synthetic and image-classification unlearning experiments in Section 5 and Appendix F, including accuracy, membership inference, relearn time and forget scores.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experimental results in Section 5 and Appendix F.

M1.justification: Section 4 and Algorithm 1 retain the same surrogate Hessian estimation, Newton update, Gaussian noise calibration and heuristic KL estimation procedures. Terminology edits do not change the method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same synthetic Gaussian data, CIFAR-10, StanfordDogs, Caltech256, MNIST and USPS. Random forgetting, class forgetting and cross-dataset surrogate scenarios are retained.

E2.justification: Retrain and Unlearn (+) remain the same comparators in the corresponding experiments. The Original model rows in Appendix F are also unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 5 and Appendix E retain the same splits, forget ratios, architectures, metrics and training/sampling settings. Removing an interpretation of relearn time does not change its evaluation protocol.

E4.justification: The covariance and Dirichlet sweeps, forget-ratio and architecture studies, and Appendix F comparisons of exact/reference versus heuristic KL and noise estimates are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same statements about multiple trials with different seeds, error bars in Appendix F figures and uncertainty entries in Tables 8–9. No statistical reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: Tables 1–9, Figures 1–4 and numerical findings in the prose are unchanged. Table 6 retains the relearn-time results despite deletion of a sentence interpreting them.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, assumptions, bounds, propositions and proofs in Sections 3–4 and Appendices A–D are unchanged. Replacing 'KL distance' with 'KL divergence' changes terminology only.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the same claims about surrogate-based certified unlearning, distance-dependent guarantees, practical approximation and preserved utility.

C2.justification: In Section 5, 'Unlearning Across Model Architectures,' v3 deletes the assertion that the RT metric implies successful removal of the forget samples' influence. This locally narrows the interpretation of Table 6; other interpretations and certification caveats remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix E retains the same hyperparameters, SGLD sampling details and variational-network training settings. The Software section provides the same two code-access links.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, cited works, reference list and novelty positioning are unchanged. Citation passages that cross column boundaries remain present.

P1.justification: Several passages in Sections 4.2 and 5 and Appendix F replace 'KL' or 'KL distance' with 'KL divergence.' One experimental interpretation sentence is removed, while section ordering and narrative structure remain intact.

P2.justification: The wording edits cause limited text reflow, spacing adjustments and column/page-break changes, particularly on pages 5 and 8–9. Figures, tables and Algorithm 1 retain their displays, captions and structure.

improvement.justification: v3 modestly refines KL terminology and removes one RT-based assertion of successful forgetting in Section 5. These local edits leave the experimental evidence, theoretical arguments, reproducibility information and substantive caveats about heuristic certification unchanged, producing no meaningful difference in overall paper quality.
